Industry/Policy Risk: Business highly dependent on road and bridge projects undertaken or awarded by governmental authorities; any change in government policies resulting in decrease in projects adversely affects business

Project Risk: Infrastructure projects involve long-term agreements (up to 3 years in EPC contracts and around 25 years in DBFOT road projects) with inherent risks including inflation, interest rate movements, liquidity, commodity and oil prices, governance, construction delays, material shortages, unanticipated cost increases and cost overruns, and disagreements with joint venture partners

Increasingly bidding for large-scale infrastructure projects carrying execution risks including potential for larger cost overruns and their effect on operating margins, and risk of default by Joint Venture Partners

outlook.statement: India's infrastructure market size is estimated at around US$ 190.51 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow to approximately US$ 205.96 billion in 2026, expanding further at a CAGR of around 8% through 2031. India's logistics market, valued at Rs. 19,53,732 crores (US$ 228.4 billion) in 2024, is projected to reach Rs. 36,73,530 crores (US$ 428.7 billion) by 2033, at a CAGR of 6.5%. The construction market in the country continues to be among the largest globally, with construction output expected to grow at an average of around 7.1% each year.

The government continues to drive the National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) combined with other initiatives such as 'Make in India' and the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme to augment the growth of the infrastructure sector. In the Union Budget 2025-26, the capital investment outlay for infrastructure was increased to Rs. 11.21 lakh crore (US$ 128.64 billion), amounting to 3.1% of GDP.

Our vision is to achieve a leadership position in India and explore opportunities beyond India. We are committed to building long-term relationships based on integrity, performance and value, as well as client satisfaction, and to be one of the premier infrastructure companies in India, executing various verticals of construction activity with the help of its in-house raw material production.

India's infrastructure sector continues to be a key structural growth driver, supported by sustained government capex, expanding project pipeline, and policy support through National Infrastructure Pipeline and PM Gati Shakti. Construction industry projected to grow at healthy pace; infrastructure-linked sectors could see 12-18% CAGR earnings growth through 2026-28. Company well positioned given track record, diversified capabilities, and financial self-reliance. Intends to strengthen order book through selective bidding for larger municipal/state contracts, deepen execution capabilities, and explore JV opportunities for large-scale projects.
